Vulnerability Management

Estrategia de mitigación

A structured approach involving technical, administrative, or procedural controls to reduce the likelihood or impact of cryptographic or PKI-related vulnerabilities, threats, or attacks.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Estrategia de mitigación?

In this glossary, Estrategia de mitigación refers to: A structured approach involving technical, administrative, or procedural controls to reduce the likelihood or impact of cryptographic or PKI-related vulnerabilities, threats, or attacks.

How is Estrategia de mitigación used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Una estrategia de mitigación sólida para PKI incluye autenticación fuerte, acceso de privilegios mínimos y monitorización continua para defenderse contra el abuso de certificados."

Why does Estrategia de mitigación matter in cybersecurity?

Estrategia de mitigación matters because it supports clear communication in Vulnerability Management contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Who uses Estrategia de mitigación?

Estrategia de mitigación is mainly used by SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, MITRE ATT&CK and published by Protermify Cybersecurity as a static cybersecurity reference page.

Definition

A structured approach involving technical, administrative, or procedural controls to reduce the likelihood or impact of cryptographic or PKI-related vulnerabilities, threats, or attacks.

Operational example

A robust mitigation strategy for PKI includes strong authentication, least-privilege access, and continuous monitoring to defend against certificate abuse.
